The Xalam Analytics market brief for the EU-funded D4D Hub (July 2025) names the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027, built around five focus areas (digital infrastructure, platforms, services, literacy and skills, innovation and entrepreneurship), and the stated period covers the brief's date, which is used as as_of since none other is given. The Electoral Reform Technical Committee's report to the Electoral Commission of Zambia says Government "has formulated" the National Digital Transformation Strategy, 2023-2027, to establish a coordinated approach to building the digital economy through adoption of digital technologies across all sectors of the economy and to support service delivery and public sector management; it names no approving act or body, and the report's submission date is used as as_of since no date of formulation is given.
The same report states the period of the National Digital Transformation Strategy as 2023-2027, which covers the report's submission date of April 2025. Text public: not stated

The strategy's own text, published by the Ministry of Technology and Science with a foreword by its Minister, says the Strategy "has been formulated" and "prepared through a multi-stakeholder approach" as the framework to guide digitalisation across public and private institutions and all sectors of the economy; it names no approving act or body, and the Ministry's publication date of 12 October 2023 is used as as_of since the text carries no adoption date.

The text is the Strategy itself, hosted on the Ministry of Technology and Science's site, and states the period 2023-2027 (five-year implementation framework, results targets for 2026), which covers its publication date of October 2023. Text public: yes

The Strategy states that the ministry responsible for technology and science "shall coordinate implementation" as the national coordinating agency and is responsible for quarterly monitoring and reporting, with Cabinet Office to give policy guidance and oversight and the E-Government Division to coordinate platforms and services in the public sector.

The Strategy says it will be financed by the Government in collaboration with cooperating partners and civil society, with budgetary allocation as the major domestic source and licensing fees and penalties to augment it, but it states no allocation, amount or budget line.

The Strategy sets out a five-year implementation framework of interventions with numeric targets, performance indicators and lead institutions for its five pillars (for example 998 communication towers, 200 district digital transformation centres, 12 sectoral digital strategies) and a results framework with 2026 targets; the text as held states no cost against the interventions.
